messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to use web images directly with renderImage()?
parts:
Just want to point out that this is a very bad habit to get into:





  output$image = renderPrint({
    src = input$image_url



    cat(sprintf('<img src=%s></img>', src))



  })

This is far safer:



  output$image = renderUI({


    src = input$image_url
    tags$img(src=src)


  })

The problem with the first snippet is that in the future we will add 1) authentication, and 2) the ability to control inputs via URL parameters. So someone could get you to click on a link like this:

http://yourserver/yourapp/?input.image_url=><script>sendCookieToEvilServer(document.cookie)</script>

which would allow whoever owns the evil server to log in to the Shiny Server instance as you (at least temporarily). This is a textbook cross site scripting vulnerability, which is caused by user-generated content being inserted indiscriminately into secure web pages.

The second snippet doesn't have this problem, because when you use Shiny's HTML building functions like tags$img, attribute values are properly escaped. So the img tag won't succeed in loading an image, but it also won't allow JavaScript to be inserted into the page no matter what the attacker puts into input$image_url.

We'll try to have this stuff written up, as I'm sure many/most Shiny users have not had to worry much about secure web coding practices before.
